span.label: Two asymptotic-normality results for random forests can look qualitatively the same and differ on whether the subsample grows fast enough for the squared bias to vanish faster than the variance. When it does not, the Gaussian limit is real and the confidence intervals built from it do not cover. A reader taking 'asymptotically normal' as the licence for an interval has no way to see this from the claim alone.

span.label: evaluation - FOR A CAUSAL ESTIMAND THE STANDARD MACHINE-LEARNING SENSE IS UNAVAILABLE: only one potential outcome per unit is ever observed, so 'direct test-set evaluation is in general impossible' and asymptotic theory does the work that held-out prediction error does elsewhere

span.label: sample splitting - AS COSTED HERE: the usual objection is that it wastes half the training data, and the answer is that the waste is per TREE and recovered across the ENSEMBLE, since the I/J split is re-randomised over each subsample so every point serves both roles in some tree
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `honesty` - A MORAL WORD GIVEN A BICONDITIONAL DEFINITION, AND THE DEFINITION IS A PROHIBITION ON DOUBLE USE. `A TREE IS HONEST IF, for each training example i, IT ONLY USES THE RESPONSE Yi TO ESTIMATE THE WITHIN-LEAF TREATMENT EFFECT τ ... OR TO DECIDE WHERE TO PLACE THE SPLITS, BUT NOT BOTH.` **Nothing about the definition is moral** - it forbids using one observation twice for two purposes. The name imports an intuition (a tree that does not cheat) that the formal content neither needs nor supports, and it travels: a reader meeting `honest trees` in a later paper will reconstruct the intuition, not the disjunction. This record is the second half of the typology's mechanism 25 - `athey2016` -> `wager2018` tightening this very term. **STAGED-TEXT NOTE:** LaTeX-adjacency fusion in the staged text, declared rather than hidden: `responseYi` is `response Y_i` and `effectτ` is `effect τ`, the space lost where prose meets a math symbol. The span is kept because it is the paper's ONLY statement of the definition and the fusion is legible; re-slicing around the symbols would remove the quantifier the definition turns on. `word_join_damage` is a declared field on `claim_relations` but NOT on `senses`, and the gate's allow-list refused it - correctly, since inventing a field per layer is how `_note` and `correction` became invisible rows. The disclosure lives here instead.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `double-sample tree` - THE NAME DESCRIBES THE MECHANISM AND NOT THE PROPERTY IT BUYS. `Our first algorithm, WHICH WE CALL A DOUBLE-SAMPLE TREE, ACHIEVES HONESTY BY DIVIDING ITS TRAINING SUBSAMPLE INTO TWO HALVES.` Honesty is the requirement; two samples is one way to meet it. **A name for the means, in a paper whose theorems are all about the end** - which is why `honesty` and `double-sample` are not interchangeable even though this paper's only honest algorithm is a double-sample one.

span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The condition is named first and realised second: 'Double-sample trees, as defined in Procedure 1, CAN ALWAYS BE USED TO BUILD HONEST TREES', and propensity trees give 'a simple recipe for building honest trees WITHOUT SAMPLE SPLITTING' - so one condition has two constructions, only one of which splits the sample.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: subsample size —causes→ confidence intervals
span.note: differs in: THE RATE AT WHICH THE SUBSAMPLE GROWS. 'the bias of the random forest decays as 1/sqrt(s_n), while its variance decays as s_n/n. IF s_n/sqrt(n) -> 0, the squared bias decays SLOWER than the variance, and so confidence intervals built using the resulting Gaussian limit distribution WILL NOT COVER' the target. Two asymptotic-normality results for random forests differ on this one exponent and on nothing a reader would notice from the statement of either theorem · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER NAMES THE PARAMETER ITS DISAGREEMENT TURNS ON AND SAYS WHAT GOES WRONG: 'although the result of Mentch and Hooker [2016] MAY APPEAR QUALITATIVELY SIMILAR TO OURS, IT CANNOT BE USED FOR VALID ASYMPTOTIC STATISTICAL INFERENCE'. A Gaussian limit is not by itself a licence to build an interval - the bias has to vanish faster than the standard error, which is a condition on a tuning parameter, not on the theorem.
